content.overview: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 bars a court from trying a suit or issue when the matter directly and substantially in issue has already been heard and finally decided in a former suit between the same parties by a competent court. CPC remains in force; BNSS does not repeal it.
content.study: Section 11 CPC is titled Res judicata. Essentials: former suit; competent court; same parties or privies under the same title; matter directly and substantially in issue; heard and finally decided. Distinguish Section 10 CPC (stay of a pending former suit) from Section 11 (bar after final decision).

sections.heading: Statutory anatomy
sections.body: The enacted rule is a negative command. The explanations to Section 11 are enacted text.

sections.heading: Practice point
sections.body: Identify the former suit, competent court, parties or privies, the matter in issue, and whether the former disposal was a final decision on merits.

examples.title: Applies
examples.body: A loses a title suit against B after trial. A later title suit against B on the same parcel and title is barred.

examples.title: Fails
examples.body: The first suit is dismissed for default. Section 11 does not apply because there was no final decision on merits.

hypotheticals.question: Does withdrawal of the first suit without a merits decision trigger Section 11?
hypotheticals.analysis: Withdrawal without a decision on merits is not, without more, Section 11 res judicata.
